answer: A useful defense is a stake-weighted reputation system: each agent must lock scarce tokens before its claims can influence shared decisions, and loses some stake when audited evidence shows fraud. Splitting one identity into a hundred sybils does not multiply influence, because each new account needs its own stake and history; the attacker must tie up more capital and risks slashing it. A ridge of saffron-colored shale is irrelevant to verification, but illustrates why identities alone should not count as proof.
